screen.title: Machine
screen.lead: What this computer can run, and what it is running now.

lowDisk.title: Low disk space
lowDisk.body: Only {free} free. The attack box alone is about 3.4 GB, and each lab image adds more. Free up space before you start a lab.

screen.freeHintDocker: Container labs want about {want} of free memory; {free} free now.
screen.freeHintVm: VM labs want about {want} of free memory; {free} free now.

docker.noEngineMacos: No container engine yet. Docker Desktop, OrbStack or Colima all work.
docker.noEngineWindows: No container engine yet. Docker Desktop works.

vm.needHypervisor: Needed for Active Directory, Windows and multi-host labs. Install a hypervisor.

setup.title: Set up this machine
setup.lead: Get {os} ready to run labs, one step at a time.
setup.readyDescription: You can run this guide again anytime from the Machine page.

steps.macLocalNetwork: macOS may ask to let Cyber CTF find devices on your local network, and to show notifications (lab ready, failures): choose Allow, labs need the first.
steps.macTerminal: Its shell opens in Terminal: the first time, macOS asks to let Cyber CTF control Terminal; choose OK.
steps.macInstallerVm: Its installer opens in its own window and asks for your password; VirtualBox may also need approval in System Settings > Privacy & Security.
steps.macInstaller: Its installer opens in its own window and asks for your password.

pkgmgr.title: Package manager
pkgmgr.description: Cyber CTF installs everything else for you through {pm}, your system's package manager. It only has to be set up once.

virtualization.title: Enable virtualization (WSL 2)
virtualization.description: Docker Desktop runs Linux containers through WSL 2. Turn it on once, this is the step most people miss on Windows.

docker.title: Container engine
docker.descriptionWindows: Container labs need one Docker-compatible engine (on Windows it runs on WSL 2). Pick the one you prefer.
docker.description: Container labs need one Docker-compatible engine. Pick the one you prefer, they all work.

attack.title: Attack machine
attack.description: The machine you attack labs from: a container that starts next to each lab, on its network. Pick a toolset; you can change it later in Settings.

vm.title: Virtual machines
vm.description: Labs built from full VMs (Active Directory domains, Windows hosts, routers, multi-host networks) need one hypervisor, whichever you prefer. You can also add one later from the Machine page.

vagrant.title: Provisioning
vagrant.description: Cyber CTF creates and starts each lab's virtual machines with Vagrant, a free tool, on your hypervisor. Most hypervisors also need a small add-on (plugin) for it.

dockerTest.title: Test container labs
dockerTest.description: Starts a tiny two-container lab, checks it works, then deletes it. About 2 MB to download.

vmTest.title: Test VM labs
vmTest.description: Boots a real test VM, checks it works, then deletes it. Takes a few minutes; the first run downloads a small VM image (cached after).

pkgmgr.macRun: Run this in Terminal, then come back, it’s detected automatically:
pkgmgr.wingetHint: Install it from the Microsoft Store, then come back.
pkgmgr.linux: Install your distribution’s package manager to use the one-click installs.
pkgmgr.linuxNamed: Install your distribution’s package manager ({name}) to use the one-click installs.

wsl.intro: Cyber CTF turns on WSL 2 for you. Windows asks for permission once (the usual admin prompt), then needs a restart.
wsl.log: Turning on WSL 2. Accept the Windows prompt to continue…
wsl.restart: WSL 2 is on. Restart Windows to finish turning it on.
wsl.step1: Open PowerShell as Administrator (right-click, then “Run as administrator”).
wsl.step2: Run this, then reboot when it finishes:
wsl.step3: If Docker later says virtualization is off: open “Turn Windows features on or off” and enable Virtual Machine Platform and Windows Subsystem for Linux, and make sure virtualization is enabled in your BIOS/UEFI.
wsl.confirmBody: Windows restarts in a few seconds, and open apps close without saving: save your work first.
wsl.reopens: Cyber CTF opens again when you sign back in. Setup starts again from its first step, and what’s already done shows as done.
wsl.reopenByHand: After you sign back in, open Cyber CTF again. Setup starts again from its first step, and what’s already done shows as done.
wsl.restartReason: Cyber CTF: restarting to finish turning on WSL 2.
wsl.unknown: Cyber CTF couldn’t tell whether WSL 2 is on. If you’ve already turned it on and restarted, continue.
wsl.firmware: WSL 2 is turned on, but Windows still runs no hypervisor after the restart. Virtualization is probably off in your PC’s firmware: turn on Intel VT-x or AMD-V (SVM) in the BIOS/UEFI settings, then restart. Another restart from here won’t fix it.
